Wide Technology Championship Picks: Griffin, Hughes Lead The Way Sergey Demidov Head of News Department Fact checked by: Sol Fayerman-Hansen Updated: Nov 3, 2026, 12:39 p.m. Published: Nov 3, 2026, 12:39 p.m. 8 min read Editorial Standards Why Trust Us? El Cardonal at Diamante has produced winning scores of 27, 24 and 29 under in its three years on the PGA Tour, so this week is a putting contest. Defending champion Ben Griffin and Canadian Mackenzie Hughes both arrive off top-five finishes in Mexico. The form guide, course history and picks for the World Wide Technology Championship. Two players stand out before a ball is struck in Cabo. Ben Griffin set the tournament record here last year at 29 under par, and Mackenzie Hughes is coming off a top-five finish. Both finished at 19 under, tied for fourth, at the VidantaWorld Mexico Open on Sunday. The case for each is stronger than the case for anyone else in the field. Where And When The World Wide Technology Championship is played from Thursday, November 5, to Sunday, November 8, at El Cardonal at Diamante in Los Cabos, a par-72 course measuring 7,452 yards. The purse is $6 million and the winner takes 500 FedExCup points. This is the sixth of eight FedExCup Fall events, and finishing inside the top 100 in the standings is what secures a PGA Tour card for 2027, so many players in the field have something on the line. Course History: Bring The Birdies Erik van Rooyen won the first edition at El Cardonal in 2023 at 27 under. Austin Eckroat followed at 24 under in 2024, and Griffin shot 259 last year to beat Chad Ramey and Sami Välimäki by two. The pattern is clear: this is no week for grinders, and any pick needs a recent record of going low. WWT Championship By The Numbers 29 Under: Griffin's Tournament Record Ben Griffin won here last year two shots clear of Ramey and Välimäki. Statistics 24 Under Or Better For Every Winner Van Rooyen won at 27 under in 2023 and Eckroat at 24 under in 2024. Statistics $6 Million Purse At El Cardonal The winner also takes 500 FedExCup points. Statistics 19 Under For Griffin And Hughes Both tied for fourth at the Mexico Open last week. Statistics Form Guide (Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images) Andrew Novak ran away with the Mexico Open at 25 under, five clear of Kristoffer Ventura and Steven Fisk. Hughes and Griffin were next at 19 under, with Van Rooyen at 18 under. The week before, Austin Smotherman won the Butterfield Bermuda Championship at 16 under, where Hughes finished at 9 under. Among the other names near the top of the market, Ben James finished at 15 under in Mexico and at 22 under at the Bank of Utah Championship, while Keith Mitchell was one shot behind Michael Brennan at the Baycurrent Classic in Japan, where Ryan Gerard finished at 13 under. The Canadians In Cabo Hughes is the Canadian to follow this week. His scoring jumped from 9 under in Bermuda to 19 under in Mexico, and that is the direction worth backing on a course that demands low numbers. Nick Taylor, Taylor Pendrith and Adam Svensson are also in the field, but Hughes is the one arriving with the form. Odds Watch Canadian sportsbooks had not posted World Wide Technology Championship markets as of Tuesday morning, November 3. 1xBet, 20Bet, Granawin, 22Bet, BetLabel, Tonybet and 29Black had no outright prices up for the event at that point. Griffin, Gerard, James and Jackson Koivun look likely to head the board when they arrive. The test for Griffin is simple: anything in the mid-teens or longer is worth taking for a defending champion in this kind of form. Keep an eye on sports betting lines through the week as Canadian prices are posted, especially for Hughes in the outright and top-20 markets. BET THE WWT CHAMPIONSHIP AT 1XBET World Wide Technology Championship Picks Griffin is the pick to win. A record score here last year, a top-five finish last week and a course that rewards exactly what he did on Sunday make him the most complete case in the field. Hughes is the second pick, best played in the top-10 or top-20 markets once they open. Van Rooyen is the long shot with course form behind him, a past winner who just went 18 under. The one to be wary of is any favourite whose recent scores have not reached the high teens, because that is roughly the floor for contention on this course.
